message.content:
Below are two ways to spin up a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU** and boots from **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ **Important**  
> * Google Cloud does **not** use the “EC2” terminology – that’s AWS.  
> * You must have a Google Cloud project with billing enabled, the **Compute Engine API** turned on, and the **NVIDIA GPU driver** installed on the VM after it comes up.  
> * The RTX A6000 is available as the GPU type `nvidia-tesla-a6000`.  
> * The instance must be created in a zone that supports GPUs (e.g., `us-central1-a`, `europe-west4-a`, etc.).

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# 1️⃣  Set variables
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # pick a GPU‑enabled zone
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"  # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM (adjust as needed)
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a6000"

# 2️⃣  Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --accelerator="type=$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT" \
  --image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts" \
  --image-project="ubuntu-os-cloud" \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-standard \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --scopes="https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"

# 3️⃣  (Optional) Install NVIDIA drivers automatically
#    The startup script below installs the driver on boot.
```

### `startup.sh` – install NVIDIA driver on boot

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Update package lists
apt-get update

# Install prerequisites
apt-get install -y build-essential dkms

# Install NVIDIA driver (the latest supported for RTX A6000)
# The driver version may change; check the latest at:
# https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/gpus/install-drivers-ubuntu
NVIDIA_DRIVER_VERSION="535.54.03"   # example; adjust if newer
wget https://us.download.nvidia.com/tesla/${NVIDIA_DRIVER_VERSION}/NVIDIA-Linux-x86_64-${NVIDIA_DRIVER_VERSION}.run
chmod +x NVIDIA-Linux-x86_64-${NVIDIA_DRIVER_VERSION}.run
./NVIDIA-Linux-x86_64-${NVIDIA_DRIVER_VERSION}.run --silent

# Reboot to load the driver
reboot
```

> **Tip:** If you prefer to install the driver manually after SSH‑ing into the VM, run:
> ```bash
> sudo apt-get update
> sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
> ```

---

## 2. Using the REST API (JSON)

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine API directly (e.g., from a script or a CI/CD pipeline), use the following POST request.

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
Authorization: Bearer {ACCESS_TOKEN}
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "projects/{PROJECT}/zones/{ZONE}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/{PROJECT}/zones/{ZONE}/diskTypes/pd-standard"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {
          "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT",
          "name": "External NAT"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{PROJECT}/zones/{ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y build-essential dkms\nNVIDIA_DRIVER_VERSION=\"535.54.03\"\nwget https://us.download.nvidia.com/tesla/${NVIDIA_DRIVER_VERSION}/NVIDIA-Linux-x86_64-${NVIDIA_DRIVER_VERSION}.run\nchmod +x NVIDIA-Linux-x86_64-${NVIDIA_DRIVER_VERSION}.run\n./NVIDIA-Linux-x86_64-${NVIDIA_DRIVER_VERSION}.run --silent\nreboot"
      }
    ]
  },
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false
  }
}
```

### Steps to use the REST API

1. **Obtain an OAuth 2.0 access token** with the scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform`.  
   ```bash
   gcloud auth application-default print-access-token
   ```
2. Replace `{PROJECT}`, `{ZONE}`, and `{ACCESS_TOKEN}` with your values.  
3. Send the request (e.g., with `curl` or Postman).  
   ```bash
   curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d @instance.json \
     "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/instances"
   ```

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|---|------|
| ✅ | Project with billing enabled |
| ✅ | Compute Engine API enabled |
| ✅ | GPU‑enabled zone selected |
| ✅ | `nvidia-tesla-a6000` accelerator added |
| ✅ | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image (`ubuntu-2004-lts`) |
| ✅ | Startup script installs NVIDIA driver (or install manually later) |
| ✅ | Proper scopes (`cloud-platform`) for the instance |

Once the instance is running, SSH into it:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu --project="$PROJECT" --zone="$ZONE"
```

Verify the GPU:

```bash
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version. 🎉

Feel free to tweak the machine type, disk size, or GPU count to match your workload. Happy GPU computing!
